justifications.c1: Several independent per-incident figures: Aster Healthcare £1.04m + £184,513 costs (search-confirmed, unserviced TMV), housing association £135k, Scottish care home £30k; but the only NHS hospital case is £8k (2008) and servicing spend is ≤~£50/valve/yr (researcher estimate), so payback per site is unproven.
justifications.c2: Six-monthly full clean and check of all TMVs (Powys tender, search-confirmed), monthly sentinel temperature checks (HSE archive), D08 first in-service test at 6-8 weeks (provider), pre-bath manual checks (NHS Lothian); recurring tasks, but no TMV failure rate.
justifications.c3: Quantified paid workaround from public procurement: GSTT TMV contract £780k ex VAT over 3 years, Powys £87,240, E&N Herts £80k, Northampton £250k water hygiene; whether monitoring can reduce these visits is untested (no guidance allows extended intervals).
justifications.c4: HTM 04-01 D08 (NHS England) and Welsh WHTM require in-service testing; NHSEI estates alert shows valves failing audit; scald prosecutions under H&S law (Aster corporate manslaughter with falsified temperature records, HA £135k, Scotland, Wales, NHS trust).
justifications.c5: NHS Jobs adverts for Band 7 Water Safety Manager / Responsible Person (Water) under HTM 04-01 (Essex, Royal Berkshire, Royal Free) and trusts buy TMV servicing and remote temperature monitoring as tendered contracts; NHS procurement is slow and IT approval is unaddressed.
justifications.c6: Water-hygiene contractors visit every valve at least six-monthly under trust contracts, but no evidence they sell monitoring, and they earn from the visits the product aims to reduce.
justifications.c7: Paying customers proven (remote temperature monitoring contract £120,156/5 yrs; FM Mattsson subscription; IW, Aquaflush, Orion) but crowded, and Factorylab ClipR already markets clip-on LoRaWAN TMV scald warning and predictive maintenance; no prices found.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN water-temperature monitors (Wavetrend) and Factorylab's clip-on delta-T sensors show feasibility; 5-yr battery is a vendor claim; no BOM; clamp-on surface readings of a 44°C threshold risk lag/false alarms.
justifications.c9: Monthly temperature checks and six-monthly servicing recur indefinitely (HSE archive, tenders) and trusts pay multi-year monitoring contracts (£120k/5 yrs ≈ £24k/yr); record-retention schedule itself not cited.
justifications.c10: Enforcement cases in trade press (SHP, The Care Home Environment), NHSEI alert, NHS trust FOI on scalds, IOSH forum thread, Health Estate Journal; forum item is practitioner interest rather than a complaint.

weakest: The servicing cost the sensor targets is only about £50 per valve per year, no guidance lets monitored valves move to longer servicing intervals, and Factorylab already sells clip-on TMV scald monitoring.
